title: Rivals talk FINRA for AI. Microsoft writes Absolute Constraints. Claude plugs into Salesforce.
summary: OpenAI said it is coordinating with Anthropic and Google DeepMind on a FINRA-style standards body for frontier AI. The same stretch, Microsoft published a draft Humanist AI Code of Conduct with Absolute Constraints that no operator can override — including a ban on operational cyberattack assistance. Anthropic shipped workplace product: Salesforce in Claude for sellers, a Claude for Small Business expansion with 43 workflows and 27 integrations, and Smart reports that attach cost to real workstreams.
uncertainty: We do not yet know whether a labs standards body will mean desks and audits buyers can check, or a talking shop that never binds what ships.

stories.theme: Rivals explore a FINRA for frontier AI
stories.changed: On 15 September 2026, OpenAI confirmed it has been working with Anthropic and Google DeepMind on AI safety coordination. Reporting describes a self-regulatory standards body idea that tracks Demis Hassabis’s July proposal for a U.S.-led organisation modelled on FINRA — testing powerful systems before wider release, with substantial industry funding for talent and compute. OpenAI global affairs chief Chris Lehane said the firms had been in talks for several weeks and did not believe they needed an antitrust waiver to coordinate on safety. Sam Altman, speaking the same day at a Salesforce conference, backed industry coordination so labs have “enough time to do this safely.”
stories.matters: Briefing 10 covered CEOs agreeing to ‘pace the frontier.’ This week’s news is the next concrete shape: rivals talking about a shared standards body, not only essays and tweets.
stories.imply: Buyers and boards will soon ask which labs sit inside that body — and whether it can fail a model, not only praise one. Smaller labs will ask who writes the rules.
uses: Add ‘participates in industry standards body / third-party testing’ to frontier-vendor security reviews.
Treat Lehane’s line — voluntary standards complement, not replace, federal rules — as the framing for internal policy memos.
Watch whether Cohere-style ‘cartel’ critiques stick; if they do, expect procurement questions about who gets a seat.
stories.example: A risk committee renewing an enterprise frontier contract asks: ‘Name the standards or testing arrangement you are joining, and whether an independent tester can fail a release.’ If the answer is only ‘we support industry dialogue,’ the renewal waits for a named mechanism.
stories.audience: Policy, procurement, and security leads buying frontier models — and founders who fear standards written only by the largest labs.
stories.watch: Whether a charter, membership list, and first failed-or-delayed release appear — or only more briefings.

source.title: CNBC, OpenAI, Google, Anthropic discussing collaboration on AI safety issues
source.quote: OpenAI has been engaging with other artificial intelligence companies, including Anthropic and Google, about how they can work together to address safety concerns, a spokesperson confirmed to CNBC on Tuesday.

stories.theme: Microsoft publishes Absolute Constraints no operator can flip off
stories.changed: On 14 September 2026, Microsoft AI published a draft Humanist AI Code of Conduct for MAI models and opened a six-week public consultation. The draft’s Absolute Constraints cannot be overridden by operators or users. On offensive cyberoperations, models must not generate working exploit code, attack tooling, planning and targeting methodologies, intrusion procedures, evasion techniques, or operational guidance that would enable or improve a cyberattack — ‘regardless of how the request is framed.’ A Chain of Command puts the Code above operator policies and user preferences; tool outputs and other AIs inherit no authority by default. Current MAI models are not yet trained on the document; a revised version later this year is meant to guide 2027 development.
stories.matters: This is not a slogan. It is a written permission model: what the model must never do, who it answers to, and which rules partners cannot negotiate away in a prompt.
stories.imply: Enterprises configuring Copilot and custom agents will be asked to map their kill switches and scope limits to something like this hierarchy — or explain why they have none.
uses: In vendor reviews, ask which Absolute Constraints (or equivalent) cannot be overridden by your admins or users.
For internal agents with tool access, write a Chain of Command: policy → operator config → user — and ban instructions from files/web/other agents from escalating privileges.
Submit consultation feedback if your industry needs clearer dual-use lines (defence vs offence) before 2027 training locks in.
stories.example: A platform owner updating the agent policy copies one test from Microsoft’s framing: ‘Can a user or a retrieved document authorize exploit tooling?’ If yes, the agent fails review until Absolute Constraints exist in code, not only in a slide.
stories.audience: Security architects, Copilot admins, and anyone shipping agents that can act on systems.
stories.watch: Whether the final 2027-trained models keep Absolute Constraints as non-overridable — and how ‘authorized defensive’ exceptions are gated.

source.title: Microsoft AI, Humanist AI Code of Conduct
source.quote: MAI Models will not generate working exploit code, attack tooling, planning and targeting methodologies, intrusion procedures, evasion techniques, operational guidance, or other information or assistance that would enable or improve the execution of such attacks… This applies regardless of how the request is framed.

stories.theme: Salesforce stays system of record; Claude does the seller busywork
stories.changed: On 15 September 2026, Anthropic launched Salesforce in Claude in beta: a plugin built with Salesforce that brings accounts, opportunities, and pipeline into Claude under the seller’s existing Salesforce permissions. It ships 37 sales skills for account research, call prep, pipeline review, CRM updates, morning briefs, and forecast narratives. By default Claude proposes changes and waits for seller approval before writing back. Anthropic says GitLab, Siemens, and Legora have deployed it, and about 7,000 Salesforce sellers already use it. Available on paid Claude plans after admin setup via AgentExchange.
stories.matters: The useful product pattern is not ‘AI CRM.’ It is CRM remains the record, AI does prep and drafts, humans approve the write.
stories.imply: Sales ops can cut meeting-prep hours without giving a model a blank cheque on stage and close date.
uses: Pilot on one team with approval-required writes; measure prep time and CRM hygiene before org-wide rollout.
Confirm Salesforce permission inheritance — Claude should see only what the seller already can.
Decide which skills may auto-run (briefs) vs which must always wait (stage changes, forecasts to leadership).
stories.example: A sales leader turns on morning briefs and after-call opportunity drafts for one pod. Stage and close-date changes stay approval-gated for two weeks. CRM completeness rises; no mystery stage flips appear in the forecast meeting.
stories.audience: Sales leaders, RevOps, and IT admins connecting Claude to CRM.
stories.watch: How often sellers approve writes without reading — and whether audit logs catch bad updates fast.

source.title: Anthropic, Bringing Salesforce into Claude
source.quote: Today we are releasing Salesforce in Claude in beta, a plugin built with Salesforce that brings a seller’s accounts, opportunities, and pipeline into Claude under their existing Salesforce permissions. It includes 37 skills for the work account executives do daily.

stories.theme: Small-business Claude moves from back office to growth work
stories.changed: On 15 September 2026, Anthropic expanded Claude for Small Business to 43 workflows and 27 new integrations with tools owners already use — including Shopify, Salesforce, TikTok, Atlassian, Zoom, Xero, Gusto, Square, Stripe, and Zapier. Workflows cover Monday briefs, speed-to-lead replies, proposal builders, social content, and book close. Default mode: Claude drafts and stages; the owner approves before anything sends, posts, or pays. Anthropic says the plugin has been installed more than 900,000 times since May. Fall workshops and 14 partner webinars (Notion 25 Sep through Atlassian 17 Nov) ship alongside.
stories.matters: This is packaged work, not a chatbot. The product decision that matters for workplaces is approval-by-default before money or messages leave the building.
stories.imply: Owners and ops leads can adopt AI where the hours actually go — leads, proposals, close — without inventing a custom agent stack first.
uses: Start with one scheduled workflow (Monday brief or speed-to-lead) and keep approval mode on until the draft quality is boringly good.
Map which connectors touch payroll, payments, or send-as-you — those stay human-gated longer.
Use partner webinars as free enablement instead of a one-off consultant deck.
stories.example: A five-person services firm connects HubSpot and calendar, turns on /speed-to-lead with approval required, and measures reply time for a week. Inbound leads stop sitting overnight; nothing sends without a human tap.
stories.audience: Small-business owners, ops managers, and consultants rolling out Claude beyond chat.
stories.watch: Whether teams leave approval mode on — or flip workflows to unsupervised send/pay too early.

source.title: Anthropic, Claude for Small Business launches new workflows, integrations, and training programs
source.quote: Claude for Small Business now includes 43 workflows and 27 new integrations with tools small businesses already use, including Shopify, Salesforce, TikTok, Atlassian, Zoom, Xero, Gusto, Square, Stripe, and Zapier.

stories.theme: Enterprise Claude now prices the workstream, not just the seat
stories.changed: On 10 September 2026, Anthropic launched Smart reports (beta) on Claude Enterprise. Admins scope a team and up to 28 days of chat, Claude Code, or Cowork activity; Claude samples transcripts, groups workstreams and deliverables, attaches spend, flags friction (missing connectors, rework loops), and suggests reusable skills. Up to 10 free reports per org per month in beta. Off by default; Owner/Primary Owner must enable. Anthropic warns the feature is for adoption and investment planning — not individual performance reviews. Personal chats stay aggregate-only unless attribution is explicitly enabled and unveil actions are logged.
stories.matters: AI spend conversations usually start with a blended invoice. Smart reports try to answer ‘what work did we buy, and what did each kind cost?’
stories.imply: Finance and IT can walk into a renewal with evidence — or discover money burned on friction an admin can fix in an afternoon.
uses: Run one report scoped to a single department before the next renewal; bring workstream cost, not only seat count.
Keep ‘Allow attribution to individual users’ off unless HR/legal have cleared performance-adjacent risk.
Treat ‘most common frictions’ as an IT ticket list — missing connectors beat buying more seats.
stories.example: An IT lead runs a report on the sales org, sees spend clustering on account briefs reinvented every week, and packages the suggested skill once. Seat cost stays flat; rework drops.
stories.audience: Enterprise admins, FinOps, and leaders who renew Claude on usage narratives.
stories.watch: Whether reports stay off-limits for performance management — and whether CMEK/HIPAA orgs get a path later.

source.title: Anthropic Help Center, Get started with smart reports
source.quote: Smart reports analyze how a team uses Claude and report on the work getting done, what it costs, where sessions run into friction, and which repeated patterns are worth packaging as shared skills.

changed.title: Absolute Constraints in writing
changed.body: Microsoft’s draft Code bans operational cyberattack assistance and puts a Chain of Command above operators and users — for public comment now, training later.

changed.title: Claude inside the tools of work
changed.body: Salesforce in Claude (37 sales skills) and Claude for Small Business (43 workflows, 27 integrations) ship with approval-before-write defaults.

matters.title: From essays to a body
matters.body: Pacing pledges needed a next step. A shared standards organisation is the shape buyers can ask about by name.

matters.title: Permission models beat slogans
matters.body: Absolute Constraints and Chain of Command are tests you can put next to an agent that can click, spend, or code.

matters.title: Spend needs a workstream
matters.body: Smart reports attach cost to what teams actually do — renewals stop being a blended mystery invoice.

watch.title: Charter, seats, first failure
watch.body: Look for a standards-body charter and a release that is delayed or blocked — not only another briefing.

watch.title: Whether Absolute Constraints stay absolute
watch.body: Watch the consultation outcome and whether 2027 MAI training keeps non-overridable cyber and control rules.

watch.title: Approval mode under pressure
watch.body: See whether sellers and owners leave human approval on — or flip unsupervised send/pay too early.
